messages.subject: Brevdale castings - defective housings, need to act
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

Following our call, this is the formal go-ahead to act for Harrow on the Brevdale castings problem. As you know we've had a run of HX units failing in the field and the Wraysbury testing points firmly at the castings. We've now taken the decision to recall the affected units that are already with customers, which is going to be expensive.

Can you set the matter up and start work on a letter of claim under the protocol? Martin Calloway (our Quality & Production Director) will be your main point of contact on the technical side, Rebecca Lund (FD) on the numbers.

Gavin

messages.subject: RE: Brevdale castings - defective housings, need to act
messages.plaintextBody:
Gavin,

Thank you - we'll open the matter today (our ref SAW/HPE/00147). James Osei will lead day to day with Tom Gallagher assisting. We'll work up a protocol-compliant letter of claim once we have the Wraysbury report finalised and a first cut of the loss.

My initial steer: this looks strong on breach, but the contractual liability cap at clause 12 will be the battleground, so let's be careful to preserve the clause 7 argument. More once I've read the Supply Agreement.

Best, Sarah

--
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.
